Belize

4 directory entries · Research in progress

  • Garifuna↗Living community and community representation connection in national cultural reporting
    Connection & source
    Living community and community representation connection in national cultural reporting

    NICH identifies Garifuna communities as part of Belize's living heritage and names a National Garifuna Council representative on its Belize project team. This supports a present-day Belize community connection, rather than reducing Garifuna identity to an earlier Caribbean migration history or treating Garifuna and Kriol as interchangeable. Inspection: Actual HTML article dated October 22, 2024: Belize national team and Garifuna Council representative, lines 33–47; safeguarding approach, lines 52–62; author credit, lines 63–65. Related NICH 2024–25 fund entry explicitly describes a Garifuna-language resource for learners in Belize. No restricted practice or cultural instruction reproduced. Limits: Country connection only; the source does not enumerate every Garifuna settlement or define a territorial polygon. A 2024 named project representative is not asserted to hold the same office in October 2026. Garifuna and Kriol remain distinct named communities in the source.

    Belize heritage project reported October 22, 2024. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Maya↗Broader Maya access point overlapping specifically named contemporary communities
    Connection & source
    Broader Maya access point overlapping specifically named contemporary communities

    The same passage names multiple Maya linguistic groups in Belize. This broader access point overlaps the Mopan and Q'eqchi' entries, rather than denoting an additional distinct nation. Inspection: Section 2 opening geographic paragraph; NICH contemporary cultural-project pages separately checked. Limits: Maya is an umbrella; no archaeological site is assigned a modern language identity.

    Contemporary community geography in scholarship published August 8, 2025. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Mopan Maya↗Present cultural community connection in a national grant record
    Connection & source
    Present cultural community connection in a national grant record

    NICH describes Katherine Karas's Mopan Maya photographic project through her family roots in southern Belize and lists a later Mopan mentor-and-apprentice initiative. These are living cultural-community connections. They do not assign every archaeological Maya site in Belize to Mopan people. Inspection: Actual HTML fund administration and grant-cycle headings; Katherine Karas entry, lines 128–131; Stanley Peck mentorship entry, lines 159–162. No project completion or current funding is inferred. Limits: Family and cultural-program accounts do not represent all Mopan histories or priorities. Broad country geography only; no archaeological identity or boundary inferred.

    Belize Culture Fund grant cycles 2023–24 and 2024–25. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗ · Supporting source 1 ↗
  • Q'eqchi'↗Contemporary linguistic community geography in community coauthored scholarship
    Connection & source
    Contemporary linguistic community geography in community coauthored scholarship

    The authors identify Q'eqchi' and Mopan as distinct linguistic communities living predominantly in southern Belize. This is a present-community connection, rather than an inference from archaeological remains. Inspection: Publisher HTML, Section 2 geographic introduction, lines 641–643; author affiliations and August 8, 2025 publication date also checked. Limits: Selected geography only; no present population total, land boundary or legal holding adopted.

    Work published online August 8, 2025; geographic passage inspected October 21, 2026. Reviewed 2026-10-21.
